task.description: Steps 0.5+1: Confirm GH-709 open. Update ISS-0669.json status IN_PROGRESS. Read src/db/pool.zig Pool.acquire() and applyRequestStorageRouting(). Read tests/integration/ordering_consumer_test.zig to understand the workaround. Document in ISS-0669.json root_cause.details: which specific call in Pool.acquire() is unsafe under raw OS thread reentrancy, whether it is Io.Threaded that is non-reentrant or something else.

result.summary: Diagnosis complete (Category A — Pool implementation bug). Pool.acquire() is unsafe under concurrent raw std.Thread.spawn OS threads due to two distinct defects: (1) Pool.mutex is std.Io.Mutex (async-cooperative, not thread-safe for raw OS threads) — under contention two raw threads can both be granted the lock; (2) applyRequestStorageRouting() is called WHILE the mutex is held and issues up to 3 SQL round-trips via Io.Threaded, whose async I/O dispatch is keyed by task frame (not OS thread), producing I/O response misdelivery across concurrent raw threads. Misdelivered BEGIN responses leave connections in auto-commit mode; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in auto-commit acquires+releases the row lock instantly, making the same row visible to all 8 threads. No source files were modified. Diagnosis written to docs/issues/ISS-0669.json root_cause.
result.fix_approach: Replace Pool.mutex from std.Io.Mutex to std.Thread.Mutex; move applyRequestStorageRouting/maybeRedirectToTenantHost calls to OUTSIDE the mutex critical section (after popping the connection from idle_indices, the connection is exclusively owned — no lock needed for the SQL setup calls).
result.next_action: Route to TEST-RUNNER (WF-03 Step 3) — diagnosis only; no source files were changed. The fix (Pool.mutex type change + restructure) is a separate BACKEND-DEV task.
